props.caption: Shading Device Types — External Louvers, Fins, Overhangs for Philippine Solar Angles
props.description: Diagram comparing shading strategies for Philippine tropical climate (5°N-19°N): horizontal overhangs for north/south facades, vertical fins for east/west facades, egg-crate louvers for combined shading. Solar altitude at summer solstice (84-90°) and winter solstice (45-52°) shown to demonstrate shading effectiveness. External louvers reducing cooling loads 40-60% vs. internal blinds annotated per PD 1096 Rule VIII.

blocks.raw: <Callout title="Key Takeaway" type="success">Natural daylight integration with intelligent artificial lighting controls reduces energy consumption by 30–50% in perimeter zones while improving occupant visual comfort and wellbeing. PD 1096 Rule VIII and the Philippine Green Building Code establish minimum daylighting and maximum lighting power density standards; design coordination between orientation, shading, sensor placement, and control logic ensures compliance and operational efficiency in tropical climates.</Callout>

blocks.raw: <Note type="note">For tropical climates, specify daylight harvesting setpoints with ±15–20% seasonal adjustment to account for monsoon-induced variation in baseline illuminance. Manual override controls enable occupant adaptation to unexpected weather changes and personal lighting preferences.</Note>
